A.explanation: Two identical springs in series share the load extension, so total extension doubles and $k_{total} = k/2$.

B.explanation: Two identical springs in parallel share the load force, so extension halves for the same load and $k_{total} = 2k$.

C.explanation: Each vertical pair is two springs in series with $k/2$, and two such pairs in parallel double it back to $k$.

D.explanation: A parallel pair of stiffness $2k$ in series with a single spring of stiffness $k$ gives $k_{total} = 2k/3$.

hints: Notice how the load force is divided and how the extensions add in each diagram, especially counting series links versus side-by-side parallel links.
Recall that springs in series add extensions so $1/k_{total} = 1/k_1 + 1/k_2$, while springs in parallel add forces so $k_{total} = k_1 + k_2$.
Work out arrangement C as two series pairs first, then combine those two pairs as a parallel combination and compare the result with $k$.
walkthrough: Identify the connections: A is 2 in series, B is 2 in parallel, C is two series-pairs in parallel, D is a parallel pair in series with one spring.
State the rules for identical springs of constant $k$: series gives $k/2$ for two springs because extension $x$ doubles to $2x$, parallel gives $2k$ because force $F$ is shared so extension halves.
For C, each side has two springs end-to-end: $1/k_{side} = 1/k + 1/k = 2/k$, so $k_{side} = k/2$.
The two sides in C support the load side-by-side, so their stiffnesses add: $k_{total} = k/2 + k/2 = k$.
Check the others: A gives $k/2$, B gives $2k$, and D gives $1/k_{total} = 1/(2k) + 1/k = 3/(2k)$ so $2k/3$. Only the C combination equals a single spring. This is option C
